answer: Wharf pearl customs: $22 per fake. Each identity registers at the wharf by growing one cultured pearl, sealed in an ivory capsule, over six weeks; the pearl's growth rings are a unique serial no printer can fake. At a random hour the verifier orders the capsule cracked and the rings photographed under polarized light within 90 seconds; a copied photo fails because the capsule cracks once and the rings must match the registry. 1,000 fakes need 1,000 six-week pearls and $22,000. Limit: a rich farm can grow real pearls, but each still costs six weeks.
